issues.description: The problem statement UML shows Animal.messageOnFeed() as a public abstract method ("+ messageOnFeed():String"), but the solution implements it as a protected abstract method (protected abstract String messageOnFeed()). This is a visibility mismatch: the specification indicates a public API for Animal, while the solution restricts the method to protected. Students reading the UML will likely implement messageOnFeed() as public; conversely, if tests or external code were placed in a different package they would require the method to be public. This inconsistency can cause confusion about the intended visibility and may lead to mismatches between student implementations and the reference solution or tests.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the visibility consistent. Either change the reference solution to declare the method as public (public abstract String messageOnFeed();) so it matches the UML/problem statement, or update the problem description/UML to indicate the method is protected if that was intended. Recommendation: change Animal.java in the solution to `public abstract String messageOnFeed();` so students implementing a public abstract method per the UML are not confused or penalized.
